title: Crush a Django N+1 with select_related and Prefetch
summary: Take 201 queries down to 2, bring the N+1 back with filter, fix it with Prefetch, then add a review count.

turns.user: book list api is slow. debug toolbar says 201 queries for 100 books

assistant.body: TL;DR: a textbook N+1. book.author costs one query per book and book.tags.all() costs another. The best practice is select_related for the ForeignKey, which becomes a JOIN, and prefetch_related for the ManyToMany, which becomes a single IN query. That makes two in total.

turns.user: faster. but private tags (is_public=False) show up too, not ok. public only

assistant.body: Only the way tags are read has to change, so one sed does it.

turns.user: tags are gone. queries are back to 102 though

assistant.body: Apologies, my previous change undid the prefetch. prefetch_related only fills the cache that all() reads, and calling filter() runs a fresh query every time. The filter belongs in the queryset of a Prefetch object, with to_attr putting the result on its own attribute. In other words, nothing inside the loop touches the database.

turns.user: oh and they want the review count in the list too. no count() per book pls

assistant.body: Annotating with Count only adds a GROUP BY to the main query. The tags come from a separate query, so no JOIN inflates the count. The new lines capture the leading spaces and reuse them, so they land at the same depth. Inside brackets a wrong indent would still parse, but it would make the diff noisy.

sed -i '' -e 's/import Prefetch$/import Count, Prefetch/' -e 's/^\( *\)\.prefetch_related(public_tags)$/\1.annotate(review_count=Count("reviews"))\n&/' -e 's/^\( *\)"author": book.author.name,$/&\n\1"reviews": book.review_count,/' books/views.py
